items.topic: Missing validation HTTP handler — how do we unblock the `validate` command?
items.context: The item declares a dependency on `fix/dtv-validation-api`, but that backlog item returns 404 — it's gone. The validation domain (`api/domain/validation/`) has models, checkers, and an executor, but `api/main.go:80-104` wires only reference/skill/expectation/report handlers. No `POST /api/v1/references/{id}/validate` route exists. Without resolving this, `validate <reference>` has nothing to call.

options.label: Expand this item's scope to add the validation HTTP handler + route registration (keep CLI and API handler in one PR).
options.rationale: The domain layer (services, models, checkers) is already done; only `api/handlers/validation.go` + one line in `main.go` is missing. Expanding scope here is the smallest path to a working `validate` command and avoids re-creating a lost backlog item. Acceptance_allow would widen to `scenarios/development-toolchain-validator/{cli,api}/**`.

options.label: Recreate `fix/dtv-validation-api` as a blocker item and defer the `validate` CLI command until that item completes.
options.rationale: Keeps this item's scope narrow (CLI only) and preserves the original dependency model. Ships `report` and `expectation` commands now; `validate` lands in a follow-up PR. Costs another round-trip through backlog/workshop for a trivial handler.

options.label: Drop the `validate` command from this item entirely; ship only `report` and `expectation`. Let the meta-optimization team live without CLI `validate`.
options.rationale: Fastest to close this item, but leaves `dtv-meta-optimization-contract` with a known gap and contradicts the item's title.

items.context: The item description writes the reports as `report --conflicts`, `report --drift`, etc. The existing CLI uses subcommand style everywhere else (`reference list`, `connection drift`). Picking one now avoids churn later.

options.label: Subcommand-style: `report conflicts`, `report drift`, `report maturity`, `report tool-baselines`. Filters via `--reference <id>` / `--skill <id>`.
options.rationale: Matches the existing `reference` / `connection` subcommand pattern, reads naturally in help output, and makes each report independently tab-completable. `cli-steer` recommends treating each API endpoint as its own command.

options.label: Flag-style: `report --conflicts`, `report --drift`, `report --maturity`, `report --tool-baselines`, exactly as the description specifies.
options.rationale: Matches the item description verbatim. Slightly terser. Awkward because the flags are mutually exclusive and `report` alone would need to error or default to something.

items.topic: `expectation` command shape — nested groups, flat groups, or type flag?
items.context: Structural expectations and CLI assertions are separate API resources (`/api/v1/expectations/structural` vs `/api/v1/expectations/cli`) with different field sets (`Pattern`/`Required` vs `Command`/`JSONPath`/`Operator`). We need to decide how the CLI exposes them.

options.label: Nested groups: `expectation structural {list|create|get|delete}` and `expectation cli {list|create|get|delete}`.
options.rationale: Matches the item description exactly. Keeps the two resource types visibly distinct, so `--help` output stays clean. Lets each group validate its own flag set without conditional logic.

options.label: Flat groups: `expectation-structural {list|…}` and `expectation-cli {list|…}`.
options.rationale: Simpler routing (one level), but hyphenated top-level commands are unusual in this CLI and make top-level `--help` noisier.

options.label: Type-flag: `expectation list --type structural|cli` with shared subcommands and a required `--type`.
options.rationale: Most compact, but hides the different field contracts behind one set of flags and forces every subcommand to branch on `--type`. Harder to document and test.

items.topic: Scope of the `validate` command — synchronous only, or include history/async?
items.context: `docs/reference/api-endpoints.md` plans both `POST /api/v1/references/{id}/validate` (sync run + report) and `GET /api/v1/references/{id}/validate/history?limit=10`. The item description only mentions the sync path. This decision controls how much we build in v1.

options.label: Synchronous v1 only: `validate <reference>` runs the validation and prints the report. No history, no async.
options.rationale: Matches the item description, ships the critical-path capability first, and keeps the surface small. The meta-optimization prompts only need the sync path. History can land later if a user asks for it.

options.label: Sync + history: also add `validate history <reference> [--limit N]` that hits `GET /api/v1/references/{id}/validate/history`.
options.rationale: Small additional cost if the history endpoint ships with the validation handler. Useful for debugging flaky validations. Depends on D1 — history only helps if the handler exists.

options.label: Full async: return a job ID, add `validate status <job-id>` and a `--wait` flag.
options.rationale: Overkill for P2 today. Adds significant surface and has no caller. Defer unless validation runs become long-running.

items.text: Validation HTTP handler is not registered in `scenarios/development-toolchain-validator/api/main.go` (lines 80–104 wire only reference/skill/expectation/report). The domain package `api/domain/validation/` contains models, structural/CLI checkers, and an executor, so writing the handler is a thin adapter rather than a green-field implementation. This is the single biggest unknown in the plan and is the subject of D1.

Every other API endpoint the CLI needs is already implemented: `GET /api/v1/reports/conflicts`, `POST /api/v1/reports/drift` (body: `{current_hashes: {…}}`), `GET /api/v1/reports/maturity`, `GET /api/v1/reports/tool-baselines`, and full CRUD at `/api/v1/expectations/{structural,cli}`. The expectation endpoints also accept `X-Dry-Run: true` (see `api/handlers/expectation.go:86`), so `--dry-run` support on mutating commands is essentially free.

Contract Decisions section lists the four pending workshop decisions with recommended defaults. Testing Plan, Rollout, Non-goals, and Definition of Done are populated but will tighten once D1–D4 land.
